item.title: Median Nerve Slider
contact: Support shoulder/elbow/wrist; do not press directly over nerve.
forceDirection: Increase neural load at one end while decreasing it at the other, e.g. elbow extension with wrist flexion then elbow flexion with wrist extension depending on chosen slider.
item.visualCue: One end loads while the other unloads ↔ smooth rhythmic slider.

subTechniques.name: Median Nerve Slider
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Improve neural movement tolerance while minimizing sustained neural strain.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Supine with the scapula controlled and the arm supported in a median-biased neurodynamic position below the symptom threshold.
subTechniques.contact: Support the shoulder, elbow, wrist and hand; no direct pressure is applied to the nerve.
subTechniques.direction: For a slider, increase load distally with wrist/finger extension while simultaneously unloading proximally with ipsilateral cervical side-bending; then reverse the pair. The movement should be smooth and symptom-limited.
subTechniques.dosage: 5–10 slow repetitions for 1–3 sets. Start with sliders before tensioners in irritable presentations.
subTechniques.reassess: Median-biased ULNT response, symptom distribution, grip/reach and the patient's familiar task.
subTechniques.clinicalPearl: A slider should move symptoms gently, not provoke a lingering flare.
subTechniques.safetyNote: Stop with progressive weakness, persistent numbness, rapidly increasing symptoms or other neurological red flags.

subTechniques.name: Radial Nerve Slider
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Improve tolerance to radial-biased upper-limb movement without sustained tension.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Supine with the shoulder girdle supported; position the arm below the symptom threshold using the radial-bias components.
subTechniques.contact: Support the elbow/wrist and control the scapula; avoid focal pressure over the radial nerve.
subTechniques.direction: Alternate distal loading (wrist/finger flexion and forearm position consistent with radial bias) with proximal unloading using cervical movement, then reverse.
subTechniques.reassess: Radial-biased neurodynamic response, lateral arm/forearm symptoms and functional reach.
subTechniques.clinicalPearl: Use the minimum combination of components needed to reproduce the relevant response; more tension is not automatically better.
subTechniques.safetyNote: Avoid aggressive tensioning in acute nerve injury.

subTechniques.name: Ulnar Nerve Slider
subTechniques.patientSetup: Supine with the arm supported and elbow/shoulder positioned below the symptom threshold.
subTechniques.contact: Support the hand, elbow and scapula; do not compress the cubital tunnel.
subTechniques.direction: Alternate distal/proximal loading so one end is loaded while the other unloads—for example, elbow/wrist positioning with cervical side-bending in opposite phases.
subTechniques.reassess: Ulnar-biased neurodynamic response, hand symptoms and grip/function.
subTechniques.clinicalPearl: If the elbow itself is irritable, reduce elbow flexion and work from a less provocative starting position.
subTechniques.safetyNote: Stop if hand numbness/weakness increases or symptoms persist after the set.
